medicines.name: Individual anti-sickness prescription
medicines.dose: As prescribed by the oncology team
medicines.timing: Prevention, delayed-sickness and rescue timing are individually specified
medicines.note: Reconcile multi-day dosing and interactions; do not add a generic steroid course.

additional_support: Follow one written prevention, home and rescue plan. The team reconciles all steroids and interacting medicines; no generic reference is an additional prescription.

Ifosfamide cycles: mesna 360 mg/m² intravenously before each dose and at 4 and 8 hours from the START of that dose. It binds bladder-damaging metabolites; it does not prevent every kidney or neurological effect.

Hospital-prescribed fluids support urine flow and clearance. The team adjusts them to urine output, blood tests, weight and heart/kidney status; continue the prescribed protection after chemotherapy finishes. Follow individual home fluid advice.

Required after every administration. After ifosfamide/etoposide: daily injections on days 8–13 (source 0.5 million units/kg, maximum 48 million units/day for primary prevention). After vincristine/cyclophosphamide-containing treatment: pegylated injection 24–48 hours later. These support recovery of infection-fighting cells; fever still needs urgent assessment.

Use the prescribed mouth-care and constipation-prevention plan. Vincristine slows bowel movement through nerve effects; report painful constipation, vomiting or abdominal swelling promptly. Mouth care helps detect and manage damaged lining before drinking becomes difficult.

If pelvic radiotherapy is planned, additional mesna is prescribed with cyclophosphamide: 240 mg/m² intravenously before it, then 240 mg/m² intravenously or 480 mg/m² orally 4 and 8 hours from its start. Doxorubicin interruption depends on the radiation field; it is not reintroduced until at least three weeks after radiation ends. Confirm actual dates with both teams.

Confirm the current numbered administration and which drugs it contains. Review constipation prevention, mouth care, medicines and infection contacts. If pelvic radiotherapy is planned, the team prescribes additional mesna with cyclophosphamide. Confirm the timing of chemotherapy around radiation.
Follow the current prescription; an improved test result does not authorise restarting after a hold.

guidance.label: Current national regimen and reconciled local prescription

clinical_source_boundaries: Do not exceed the source doxorubicin lifetime ceiling of 375 mg/m² without specialist reconciliation of previous anthracycline exposure. The five planned 75 mg/m² doses reach that ceiling.
Mesna after ifosfamide is timed from the START of the infusion, not its finish; 360 mg/m² intravenously before, and 4 and 8 hours after the start on each treatment day.

When pelvic radiotherapy is planned, cyclophosphamide protection is mesna 240 mg/m² intravenously before it, then either 240 mg/m² intravenously or 480 mg/m² orally at 4 and 8 hours from its start. These route-dependent doses are not interchangeable.

Doxorubicin may be omitted during radiotherapy depending on the field and is not reintroduced until at least three weeks after radiotherapy ends. Vincristine product information has a separate liver-field radiation precaution.

Hospital hydration is individually prescribed. Source surveillance includes urine output at least 100 mL/hour, strict fluid balance and daily weight; positive balance above 1 litre or weight gain above 1 kg needs review. These are clinical monitoring criteria, not home fluid targets.
Current etoposide, cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide and vincristine product organ-impairment wording may differ from national tables; reconcile the supplied products and retain safety-history stops.

Assess current ifosfamide central-nervous-system toxicity separately from peripheral neuropathy. Current suspected brain toxicity requires interruption and immediate assessment; a broad nerve-toxicity grade is not proof of encephalopathy. Unresolved symptom localisation requires review. Keep each national regimen’s separate severe-event, prior-history and future-rechallenge rules; do not convert every peripheral nerve symptom into a permanent ifosfamide stop.

Current Irish Mitoxana 1 g product information (11 September 2023) lists stricter organ contraindications than the national ifosfamide dose tables: serum creatinine above 120 micromol/L, bilirubin above 17 micromol/L, or transaminases/alkaline phosphatase above 2.5 times the upper limit of normal. Confirm the actual supplied product and oncology/pharmacy reconciliation; do not assume a different product or replace the national table with a universal new dose rule.

phases.label: Days 1–5: irinotecan and temozolomide

medicines.name: Individual anti-sickness prescription
medicines.dose: As prescribed by the oncology team
medicines.timing: Prevention, delayed-sickness and rescue timing are individually specified
medicines.note: Reconcile multi-day dosing and interactions; do not add a generic steroid course.

additional_support: Follow one written prevention, home and rescue plan. The team reconciles all steroids and interacting medicines; no generic reference is an additional prescription.

Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prevention is required with this temozolomide regimen. The prescribed medicine helps prevent an opportunistic lung infection; follow its full course and report new cough or breathlessness. Hepatitis B results may require a separate expert prevention and follow-up plan.

Sweating, cramps and early diarrhoea during or soon after infusion can be a cholinergic reaction. Tell the nurse immediately. The national regimen says atropine should not be used in patients with glaucoma. Tell the treatment team if you have glaucoma. This source does not give a fixed atropine dose.

Irinotecan can cause two different bowel problems. Cramping, sweating and diarrhoea during or shortly after infusion can be an acute cholinergic reaction: tell the nurse immediately; prescribed atropine may be used. Delayed diarrhoea begins more than 24 hours later and can cause dangerous dehydration or infection. Contact oncology at the first loose stool and follow the written anti-diarrhoeal and rehydration prescription. Fever, severe pain, blood, faintness, very little urine or inability to drink needs immediate assessment; never wait for a time threshold when seriously unwell.

If a temozolomide dose is missed, contact the treatment team for instructions. Never double a dose or restart a held course yourself. If vomiting occurs after temozolomide, do not take an extra dose. Capsules must be swallowed whole, fasting, at least one hour before irinotecan.

Agree a written early-reaction and delayed-diarrhoea plan, the infection-prevention prescription, capsule timing and urgent contacts. Review all medicines and supplements; do not start antidiarrhoeals preventively or change an antibiotic yourself. If a temozolomide dose is missed, contact the treatment team for instructions. Never double a dose or restart a held course yourself.
Follow the current prescription; an improved test result does not authorise restarting after a hold.

guidance.label: Current national regimen and reconciled local prescription

clinical_source_boundaries: Document off-label indication discussion and the local governance/consent requirements stated in the national source.
Review baseline infection, bowel status and UGT1A1*28 homozygosity when known; do not invent a universal genotype-based starting-dose formula.
Renal eligibility and dose-table wording require specialist reconciliation; normal current results cannot bypass a recorded contraindication or permanent stop.
The source recovery requirement for delayed diarrhoea is strict; keep previous maximum severity, actual recovery date, cycle-day history and prescribed restart distinct.

Adult loperamide and cefixime reference doses are not paediatric prescriptions. The source adult loperamide reference is 4 mg initially, then 2 mg every 2 hours, continuing for 12 hours after the last liquid stool, but not longer than 48 hours at this dose. This requires the prescribed local adult plan and is not a paediatric dose or prophylactic instruction. Persistent diarrhoea beyond 48 hours despite this plan, fever or severe illness requires urgent reassessment/hospital care. Oral cefixime may be considered in adults at 400 mg daily from day −2 to day +7; it is not a universal or paediatric prescription.
The source day-35/one-week wording is internally inconsistent; do not silently convert it into an invented recovery deadline.
Do not import the vincristine-containing regimen’s missed-dose or temozolomide escalation rules.

Cycles 1–2: daily injections on days 4–7 and 9–11 at the prescribed 5 micrograms/kg. Cycles 3–9: pegylated growth factor may be considered from day 4. These support marrow recovery; the later plan is not automatically the same as the early plan.

The team considers Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and antifungal prevention, and any tumour-lysis precautions. These are individual decisions here. Azole antifungals can increase vincristine toxicity; pharmacy must reconcile the plan.

Confirm whether this is cycle 1–2, 3–4 or 5–9, and which vincristine appointments and doxorubicin doses apply. Check the full mesna/hydration prescription and the growth-factor calendar. Ask about individual infection prevention, bowel support and medicines that may interact.
Follow the current prescription; an improved test result does not authorise restarting after a hold.

Keep each national regimen’s separate severe-event, prior-history and future-rechallenge rules; do not convert every peripheral nerve symptom into a permanent ifosfamide stop.

Confirm the actual supplied product and oncology/pharmacy reconciliation; do not assume a different product or replace the national table with a universal new dose rule.
